name: Kailasanathar Temple, Kodaganallur
deity: Shiva as Kailasanathar, with the Goddess Sivakami
period: Third of the Nava Kailasam, the shrine of Mars; Pandya inscriptions of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries
summary: In the riverside village of Kodaganallur, whose old name recalls the serpent Karkotaka, Shiva as Kailasanathar keeps the third of the Nava Kailasam, the shrine linked with Mars.

sections.history: Kodaganallur is a village on the Tamiraparani a short way west of Tirunelveli, just south of Nadukallur on the road towards Mukkudal. Its Kailasanathar temple is the third of the Nava Kailasam and the shrine of Mars, Sevvai. Inscriptions on its walls date to the Pandya period of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, and they record the village under older names — Kodanur, and a chaturvedimangalam, a settlement granted to Vedic scholars. That learned character has stayed with Kodaganallur, a village of several old temples, among them the west-facing Abhimukteeswarar shrine on the riverbank and a temple of Vishnu.
sections.architecture: The temple is a compact Dravidian stone shrine of the Pandya country, its sanctum holding the lingam of Kailasanathar with the Goddess Sivakami in her own shrine. The inscribed walls are themselves part of its interest, carrying the record of the gifts and grants of the Pandya age. The sacred tree is the vilvam, whose leaves are offered to Shiva, and the temple's tirtham is the Tamiraparani flowing close by.
sections.legends: The village's older name was Karkotaka-nallur, after the great serpent Karkotaka of the epics — the naga who bit King Nala. Tradition holds that Karkotaka, seeking release from the burden of that deed, was told to worship Shiva on the banks of the Tamiraparani, and that his penance here won him liberation; the name wore down in time to Kodaganallur. In the Nava Kailasam story, it is where the third of the lotuses set afloat by the sage Romasa came to rest.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the monthly pradosham, the Margazhi Thiruvathirai of the dancing Shiva, and Maha Shivaratri. As the shrine of Mars in the Nava Kailasam, it draws devotees on Tuesdays. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Kodaganallur is a quiet village temple rather than a pilgrim town: a place to read the old letters cut into the walls, offer vilvam leaves, and walk down to the river. It is the third stop on the Nava Kailasam round, between Cheranmahadevi upstream and Kunnathur near Tirunelveli.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; village temples may open later and close earlier than town shrines. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Kodaganallur lies in Tirunelveli district, about 15–16 km from Tirunelveli Junction on the Tirunelveli–Mukkudal road; alight at Nadukallur and the temple is about a kilometre to the south. Tirunelveli is the nearest railway junction and Thoothukudi the nearest airport.
